import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
try:
    df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')
except FileNotFoundError:
    # Create a dummy dataframe for code execution if the file is not found
    data = {
        'brand': ['Leica', 'Fuji', 'Pentax', 'Canon', 'Nikon', 'Sony', 'Olympus', 'Panasonic'],
        'model_year': [2005, 2019, 2012, 2020, 2018, 2021, 2017, 2019],
        'megapixels': [13.5, 46.4, 38.7, 24.1, 45.7, 50.1, 20.4, 47.3],
        'max_iso': [25600, 51200, 12800, 102400, 102400, 102400, 25600, 51200],
        'weight_grams': [324, 1151, 598, 449, 915, 737, 498, 1016],
        'price_usd': [811.80, 3596.41, 3357.20, 899.00, 2999.99, 6498.00, 1199.00, 3497.99],
        'sensor_type': ['Micro 4/3', 'APS-C', 'Full Frame', 'APS-C', 'Full Frame', 'Full Frame', 'Micro 4/3', 'Full Frame'],
        'has_video_4k': [1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1],
        'lens_mount': ['E', 'EF', 'MFT', 'RF', 'Z', 'E', 'MFT', 'L'],
        'body_type': ['Compact', 'Mirrorless', 'Mirrorless', 'DSLR', 'DSLR', 'Mirrorless', 'Mirrorless', 'Mirrorless']
    }
    df = pd.DataFrame(data * 125) # Approximate 1000 rows

# Data Preparation: For clarity, focus on the most common sensor types
top_sensors = df['sensor_type'].value_counts().nlargest(4).index
df_filtered = df[df['sensor_type'].isin(top_sensors)].copy()

# Set a professional and modern style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", font_scale=1.1)
plt.rcParams['font.family'] = 'sans-serif'
plt.rcParams['font.sans-serif'] = ['DejaVu Sans', 'Arial', 'Helvetica']

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create the scatterplot
# This plot shows the relationship between Price and Megapixels.
# Color is used to distinguish between different Sensor Types.
# Bubble size represents the camera's maximum ISO, indicating low-light performance.
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df_filtered,
    x='price_usd',
    y='megapixels',
    hue='sensor_type',
    size='max_iso',
    sizes=(40, 600),
    alpha=0.7,
    palette='viridis',
    ax=ax,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=0.5
)

# Use a logarithmic scale for the x-axis to better visualize the wide price range
ax.set_xscale('log')

# Set informative title and labels
fig.suptitle(
    'Digital Camera Market Landscape: Price, Resolution, and Sensor Tech',
    fontsize=20,
    fontweight='bold',
    y=0.98
)
ax.set_title(
    'Full Frame cameras typically command higher prices and megapixels. Bubble size indicates low-light capability (Max ISO).',
    fontsize=12,
    pad=10
)
ax.set_xlabel('Price (USD) - Logarithmic Scale', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_ylabel('Megapixels (MP)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Format the x-axis ticks to be more readable (e.g., $1,000 instead of 1000)
formatter = mticker.ScalarFormatter()
formatter.set_scientific(False)
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: f'${int(x):,}'))
ax.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# Improve legend clarity and position
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Separate the hue and size legends
hue_legend_index = len(top_sensors) + 1
ax.legend(
    handles[:hue_legend_index],
    labels[:hue_legend_index],
    title='Sensor Type',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1),
    loc='upper left',
    borderaxespad=0.,
    title_fontsize='13',
    fontsize='11'
)

# Manually create a second legend for size
size_legend = ax.legend(
    handles[hue_legend_index:],
    labels[hue_legend_index:],
    title='Max ISO',
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.6),
    loc='upper left',
    borderaxespad=0.,
    title_fontsize='13',
    fontsize='11'
)
ax.add_artist(size_legend)

# Add a grid for better readability
ax.grid(which='major', linestyle='--', linewidth='0.5', color='gray')
ax.grid(which='minor', linestyle=':', linewidth='0.5', color='lightgray')

# Final layout adjustment
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 0.95]) # Adjust rect to make space for legends

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
